name: Purple toothpaste / colour corrector serum

lead: Purple toothpaste and colour corrector serums are trend products that tint the teeth so they look less yellow straight away.
No clinical studies were found, so the benefit is based on colour theory and user accounts rather than trials.

paras: The purple pigment is said to visually cancel yellow tones, like colour correction in makeup. It does not chemically whiten the tooth.
No published safety data specific to these products were found.

lead: Purple toothpastes and colour corrector serums are cosmetic dental products, popular in short-video trends, that apply a purple pigment to the teeth to give an instant whiter look. They are marketed as a peroxide-free alternative to bleaching.

The underlying idea is that violet and yellow are roughly opposite on the colour wheel, and complementary lights can combine to look neutral, though the source notes this applies to light and that pigments behave differently.[1] Peroxide whitening works by a different route, breaking down pigment molecules.[2]
No clinical studies of these products were identified.

paras: Products in this category are applied by brushing or as a serum and leave a visible violet film that proponents say offsets yellowish tooth colour.[1] Whether results persist after rinsing, eating or drinking is not documented in the published literature reviewed.
Dental references note that actual whitening typically uses peroxide agents, with results ranging from one or two shades for home products to more for in-office treatment.[2]
